scope: Read-only upstream source inspection; no Java, installer, game or UI execution. No upstream implementation copied. Source facts do not establish Windows runtime acceptance.

facts: Argument-file lexical handling consumes bytes and escapes backslash, quote and n/r/t/f inside quotes.
Application arguments after the main class are not expanded as argument files.
No UTF-8 to native-charset transcode is performed while reading the argument file.
Windows command parsing uses CharNextExA(CP_ACP). Native encoding must not be inferred from -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8.
Windows launcher command parsing starts with GetCommandLine, not the Go parent process locale.
makePlatformString decodes platform bytes using sun.jnu.encoding.
JVM_GetProperties converts command-line -D property strings using create_from_platform_dependent_str.

limitations: Only named standard Windows encodings are adapted, with a strict local round trip. Unsupported named encodings fail; absent encoding evidence permits ASCII only.
The JVM-reported sun.jnu.encoding is used first; native.encoding is a fallback, never file.encoding.
No claims of all vendor or Windows-locale compatibility; effective native encoding, Java8 manifest loading and Java9+ argument-file loading still require isolated runtime acceptance.
Unspecified Unix native encodings remain outside this Windows adaptation; existing UTF-8 transport is unchanged.
